operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The paragraph establishes the Good Conduct Medal and authorizes its award to enlisted members under regulations of the service Secretaries. Before EO 9323: Army enlisted men who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal service and are recommended by their commanders, regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 9323: restated; Army enlisted men who on or after August 27, 1940 completed three years, or after December 7, 1941 served one year during war; no commander recommendation; regulations by the Secretary of War. After EO 10444: restated; authority as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces; regulations by the Secretaries of the Army and the Air Force; Army and Air Force enlisted men; adds those with less than three years of honorable service after June 27, 1950 who were not previously awarded the medal; proviso against awards for less than one year except physical-disability separations. After EO 14085 section 2: men becomes members and Space Force is added with a December 20, 2019 start for Space Force members. The clause was amended, never ended, and the U.S. Code prints the amended text as current, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

By virtue of the authority vested in  
the Secretary of Agriculture by the De­
partment of Agriculture Appropriation  
Act, 1941, approved June 25, 1940 (54  
Stat. 532, 557; 7 U.S.C. § 231), the Ne­
braska Brand Committee is authorized to  
conduct a brand inspection service, as set  
forth in the following section, which is  
added to Part 203, Chapter H, Title 9,  
Code of Federal Regulations:
§  203.12 Nebraska Brand Committee.  
Upon a written request made to and filed  
with the Secretary of Agriculture, the  
Nebraska Brand Committee, duly organ­
ized under the laws of the State of Ne­
braska, is hereby authorized, with re­
spect to livestock originating in or  
shipped to market from the Nebraska  
brand inspection area of the State of  
Nebraska, which shall consist of all of  
that part of the State of Nebraska lying  
within the following counties: Arthur,  
Banner, Blaine, Box Butte, Boyd, Brown,  
Chase, Cherry, Cheyenne, Custer, Dawes,  
Dawson, Deuel, Dundy, Frontier, Garden,  
Garfield, Grant, Hayes, Hitchcock, Holt,  
Hooker, Keith, Keya Paha, Kimball, Lin­
coln, Logan, Loup, McPherson, Morrill,  
Perkins, Red Willow, Rock, Scotts Bluff,  
Sheridan, Sioux, Thomas, Wheeler, to  
charge and collect reasonable fees, ap­
proved by the Secretary of Agriculture,  
to be paid by the owners of the livestock  
inspected, for the inspection of brands  
appearing upon livestock sold or offered  
for sale at those markets at which the  
said Nebraska Brand Committee may  
register as a market agency, such inspec­
tion to be made to determine the owner­
ship of the livestock. Such inspection  
and charging and collection of fees shall  
be subject to the provisions of the Pack­
ers and Stockyards Act and such regu­
lations as the Secretary may from time  
to time prescribe.

Executive Order 8809 of June 28, 1941 (6 FR 3209), Good Conduct Medal, is a single operative paragraph in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8809.txt; trailing number [No. 8809], signed Franklin D. Roosevelt at The White House June 28, 1941): a Good Conduct Medal is established and may be awarded, under regulations of the Secretary of War, to enlisted men of the Army of the United States who hereafter honorably complete three years of active Federal military service and are recommended by their commanding officers. Three later orders each amend that single clause and are recorded as later events with before and after text: EO 9323 (March 31, 1943) restated the paragraph; EO 10444 (April 10, 1953) restated it again; and EO 14085, section 2 (October 3, 2022) struck and inserted words. The OFR catalog record for EO 8809 reads 'Amended by: EO 9323, March 31, 1943; EO 10444, April 10, 1953 | See: Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163)'. Both Amended by notes are addressed as later events. The See note is a cross reference to a Secretary of Defense transfer order whose text is not held; it is not a revocation note, it predates EO 10444 (which already names the Secretary of the Air Force), and I do not treat it as ending or changing the order. EO 14085, which the catalog does not list, is found in held texts and in the U.S. Code note. Search of held texts for the number EO 8809 finds the order, EO 9323, EO 10444 (and the duplicate page text under EO 10445 and EO 9324), EO 14085 and the 1989 codification; none revokes or supersedes the order. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition) prints the order as a note and records no ending statement, and the packet holds no source showing a later statute that affects it. 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note prints the order as amended by EO 9323, EO 10444 and EO 14085 section 2, as current text; the printed current text matches the text as restated by EO 10444 and amended by EO 14085.
